chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he disliked pelting the Jamarah at night, and he permitted it for the slave and the herdsman with regards to pelting the Jamarah at night.

key_terms.رَمْيَ الْجِمَارِ: Pelting the Jamarah (ritual throwing of stones)

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams permit pelting the Jamarah at night in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a general preference against pelting the Jamarah at night, yet grants a specific concession (*rukhsah*) for slaves and herdsmen. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of accommodating practical hardships (*mashaqqah*) and occupational duties, ensuring that those with less flexibility are not burdened with the strict timing preferred for the general populace.
